CFP-002.title: Event-Driven AI Pipelines on GCP: From Eventarc to LLMs
CFP-002.description: In this live building session, I will create a production-ready, event-driven AI pipeline on Google Cloud from a blank terminal to a working system. A file lands in Cloud Storage, Eventarc routes the event, Cloud Run processes it reliably, and Vertex AI with Gemini enriches the data through classification, summarization, and entity extraction. The enriched results are then stored. The focus is not on AI hype or a pre-recorded happy-path demo. Attendees will see the system being built live, including the practical decisions, trade-offs, and failure scenarios involved in making it production-ready.

CFP-012.title: The Physics of Voice: Building a Coach in Flutter with Whisper and Acoustic Analysis
CFP-012.description: Your voice is a waveform. Pitch, tempo, energy, silence — all measurable, all improvable. In this session, I'll show how I built a real-time public speaking coach in Flutter by combining acoustic physics with modern voice recognition.We'll start where most Flutter voice talks don't: the signal itself. Understanding frequency, amplitude, and phoneme structure determines which APIs you reach for, how you tune Whisper for real-world input, and why dialect — yes, Austrian German included — can silently wreck transcription accuracy. From there, we go hands-on: integrating Whisper for high-accuracy STT alongside on-device fallbacks, extracting real-time acoustic features like pitch variance, speaking rate, and filler words to deliver actionable coaching feedback, and designing Flutter UIs that feel natural when voice is the primary input.

CFP-014.title: AI Code Review: Comparing Ready-Made Tools and Building Your Own
CFP-014.description: Should your team adopt an existing AI code reviewer or build its own? I will compare both approaches using real development workflows and moreover, tell the most effective approaches in verifying the PRs by AI reviewers. We will examine CodeRabbit, Greptile, Cursor Bugbot, and Claude Code across review quality, false positives, repository context, customization, developer experience, privacy, maintenance, and cost. Using PRs with planted defects, we will see what these tools catch and miss. Next, I will show how we built DevDigest, our own AI code reviewer. We will explore its architecture, model integration, structured findings, and context pipeline: system instructions, PR intent, linked specifications and skills, a repository map, affected callers, and finally the diff. We will also integrate review with spec-driven development. Instead of checking only whether the code looks correct, the reviewer can validate whether the implementation follows the original requirements, architectural decisions, and expected behavior. The talk will cover the pros and cons of ready-made and custom solutions and caveats on our path of creating a well-functioning solution that works for our purposes. I'm also planning to integrate Antigravity and Firebase into the talk. The duration is flexible, from 30 to 60 min. 30min can be also enough.

CFP-021.title: Written by Agents. Reviewed by Nobody. Running in Production
CFP-021.description: I gave one feature to AI agents. They sent back 300,000 lines of code in one pull request. Nobody read it, and it is running in production. This talk is not about trusting the machine. It is about moving what you check. Across more than 400 companies, AI use rose 65%, but merged code changes rose only 7.76%. Reviews, handoffs and approvals absorbed the gain. Using Formula 1 as the lens, I show what replaces code review: a definition of "done" written before the work starts, tests on the real product, and team standards turned into automatic checks.

CFP-034.title: Beyond Prompt Engineering: Solving Complex Optimization Problems with AlphaEvolve
CFP-034.description: Large Language Models excel at generating standard boilerplate code, but how do we leverage them to discover novel, high-performance algorithms for complex combinatorial optimization problems? Enter AlphaEvolve—Google DeepMind's evolutionary coding framework that pairs LLMs with automated program verification to discover, evaluate, and iteratively refine code. In this talk, we will move past standard prompt engineering and explore how evolutionary compute loops turn Gemini into an engine for algorithmic discovery. Drawing from Google Cloud Professional Services Organization (PSO) deployment patterns, we will walk through setting up automated evaluation functions, defining seed algorithms, and scaling evolutionary iterations to solve real-world engineering bottlenecks—such as supply chain routing, data pipeline scheduling, and resource allocation. You will leave with a clear blueprint for deploying evolutionary AI pipelines on Google Cloud to tackle NP-hard and domain-specific system constraints.

CFP-050.title: Stop Guessing, Start Debugging (with Antigravity & Chrome DevTools MCP)
CFP-050.description: “Works on my machine” doesn’t count as debugging. In this workshop, we’ll use Antigravity and Chrome DevTools MCP to catch bugs where they actually happen—the browser. Instead of guessing, we’ll let AI access real data like network requests, console logs, and runtime state to diagnose and fix issues faster (and with less frustration). Why does this matter? Because most debugging today is based on incomplete context—we read code, make assumptions, and hope we’re right. With Antigravity and MCP, AI stops guessing and starts collaborating with real, structured data from your app. This means fewer blind spots, faster feedback loops, and more confidence that your fix actually works—not just locally, but in reality.

INVITED-001.title: Stop Chatting with Your Docs — Architecting a Local-First AI Mind Coach in TypeScript with Gemma & Gemini Argon
INVITED-001.description:
Most AI integrations for developer notes boil down to a simple "chat with your docs" wrapper. While convenient, this model creates a dangerous illusion of mastery: when AI serves ready-made summaries on demand, active thinking stops and deep learning fades away. What if we inverted this architecture in TypeScript turning our private knowledge base into a demanding Socratic coach with the absolute privacy of an offline notebook?
In this talk, we will dissect the architecture of a two-tier cognitive sparring partner that stress-tests your engineering knowledge without ever sending a single private file to the cloud:
Local Gemma (The Offline Sparring Partner): Running entirely on your machine against raw Markdown notes, it acts as a relentless coach on trains or flights driving Socratic dialogue, banning industry buzzwords, and forcing you to explain complex mechanisms in your own words using the Feynman technique.Gemini Argon (The Zero-Knowledge Judge): Stepping in when connectivity returns, we leverage Argon within a strict LLM-as-a-Judge pattern via the @google/genai SDK. Using a blind claim-extraction protocol, Argon never sees your underlying notes, only the generated challenge and your human response ruthlessly exposing logical fallacies, shallow hand-waving, and gaps in your mental model before scheduling your next review.Join this session to learn how to combine edge inference, zero-knowledge privacy patterns, and frontier reasoning with Gemini Argon to build tools that upgrade rather than replace your engineering brain.

PANEL-01.title: From 10x Coders to 10x Teams: Engineering Leadership with AI

CFP-028.title: Voice agents, hype-free: lessons from Gemini's audio stack
CFP-028.description: Voice agents are having a moment, but building one that feels responsive, useful, and not painfully awkward is still harder than the demos make it look. In this talk, I’ll walk through Gemini’s current audio stack, including Gemini Live, TTS, transcription, translation, and asynchronous tool calling, and show how the pieces fit together when you build a real voice-first experience. Rather than focusing on API basics, I’ll concentrate on the parts that become interesting in practice: latency, interruptions, long-running tools, choosing between native audio and traditional speech pipelines, and handling conversations that do not follow neat request-response turns. Expect practical demos, architectural trade-offs, and lessons learned from experimenting with the stack, including what works well, what still feels rough, and where voice agents are genuinely useful beyond the hype.
